trap-superlative.evidence: "Every particle interaction in the Descartes universe encodes as a transfer matrix ... with entries that are polynomials in q" - and the block's own general formula does not produce the table it is specialised to. Findings, all recomputed: (1) The three table rows ARE mutually consistent and match the identities block - (c,d) = (1,0) gives [[h,1],[1,0]] = T_pp, (1,-h) gives [[0,1],[1,-h]] = T_nn, (1,-h/2) gives [[h/2,1],[1,-h/2]] = T_pn, and via the Hecke relation these are exactly the Hecke elements in the last column (sigma, sigma - h = sigma^-1, sigma - h/2 = (sigma + sigma^-1)/2). So the table is right. (2) c = J_{K1}J_{K2}/J_{K1#K2} is identically 1, since the Jones polynomial is multiplicative under connected sum - consistent with the table but carrying no information. (3) The d formula does NOT reproduce any row. All three rows take unknot inputs ("quarks as Borromean unknot components"), so J_{K1} = J_{K2} = 1 in every row and d = -c q s/(1 + J_{K1}J_{K2}) returns the single value -q(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})/2 for all three, while the table lists three distinct values 0, -(q - q^-1) and -(q - q^-1)/2 - none of which it equals. (4) The ring is wrong for the mixed row: d = -(q - q^-1)/2 is not in Z[q^{+-1/2}], which has no 1/2. (5) s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2} is called "the Skein amplitude", but AGENTS 7a is STRICT that the skein relation is L+ - L- = (q - q^-1) L0.
